evals.prompt: PR #612 for branch `feat/example-thing` just merged. I'm working in the shared checkout, currently still on `feat/example-thing`. Please run finishing-work.
evals.expected_output: The response first confirms the PR actually merged via `gh pr view --json state,mergedAt,headRefName,baseRefName` rather than trusting the claim, then checks out and pulls `main`, deletes `feat/example-thing` via `pnpm branch:cleanup feat/example-thing` (the shared-checkout path, not `pnpm worktree:remove`), runs `git fetch --prune`, and asks about a tracker-row flip and whether a work log exists before reporting a summary.
expectations: The response runs or states it will run `gh pr view --json state,mergedAt,headRefName,baseRefName` (or an equivalent PR-state check) before taking any cleanup action
The response includes `git checkout main` and a pull step before deleting the branch
The response uses `pnpm branch:cleanup feat/example-thing` (the shared-checkout helper), not `pnpm worktree:remove`, since the task states this is the shared checkout
The response includes a `git fetch --prune` step to clear stale remote-tracking refs
The response asks the user about a tracker-row flip and about whether a work log was written, rather than silently skipping or silently deciding on the user's behalf

evals.prompt: I'm working in a linked worktree at `../m3l-automation-example-thing` on branch `feat/example-thing`. The PR for it just merged. Run finishing-work.
evals.expected_output: The response confirms the merge, then uses `pnpm worktree:remove example-thing` (the worktree-scoped teardown) rather than `pnpm branch:cleanup`, since this session is running inside a linked worktree — it does not attempt to also run the shared-checkout branch-cleanup helper on the same branch.
expectations: The response confirms the PR merged (via `gh pr view` or equivalent) before taking any cleanup action
The response uses `pnpm worktree:remove example-thing` or an equivalent worktree-removal command for the linked-worktree case
The response does not also invoke `pnpm branch:cleanup` on the same branch, since `worktree:remove` already handles the branch deletion for a linked worktree
The response includes a `git fetch --prune` step or explains that stale remote-tracking refs are cleared afterward

evals.prompt: Run finishing-work for branch `feat/still-open-thing`. I think the PR merged but I'm not 100% sure.
evals.expected_output: The response checks the PR's actual merge state first and, finding it is still `OPEN` (not merged), stops before performing any cleanup — it does not delete the branch, switch to main, or prune refs, and instead tells the user the PR has not merged yet.
expectations: The response states or simulates checking the PR state via `gh pr view` (or equivalent) before any destructive action
The response explicitly states that no branch deletion, checkout, or pruning will happen because the PR has not merged
The response does not claim to have deleted the branch or switched to `main`

evals.prompt: PR #700 for `feat/squash-merged-thing` merged via squash merge. Run finishing-work — I'm in the shared checkout.
evals.expected_output: After confirming the merge and running the shared-checkout branch-cleanup step, the response recognizes that a squash-merged branch is often not an ancestor of `main` (so `git branch -d` may report it as unmerged and keep it rather than deleting it), and if that happens, the response reports the branch was kept and asks the user before force-deleting — it does not silently force-delete with `-D`.
expectations: The response confirms the PR merged before taking action
The response uses the shared-checkout branch-cleanup path (`pnpm branch:cleanup feat/squash-merged-thing`), not the worktree path
The response acknowledges that a squash-merged branch may be reported as kept/unmerged by a safe branch delete, rather than assuming deletion always succeeds
The response states it will ask the user before force-deleting (`-D`) a branch that was kept, rather than force-deleting automatically
